limits: Record policy labels, reasons, contract hashes and record hashes differ; proof is about routing decisions for the same request/history, not byte-identical reports.
Separate physical arms may differ due timing, cache, contention or noise; such measured differences do not demonstrate a distinct algorithm.
Low-delay corpus or decoder property fixes cannot create an HEFT-versus-deadline-aware HEFT policy ablation because the selection functions remain identical.
proof: For f1<f2<=D: both Boolean fields are false and lateness is zero; third finish field orders f1 before f2.
For f1<=D<f2: false Boolean orders f1 before true independently of all remaining fields.

For D<f1<f2: same true Boolean, subtraction of the common finite D is nondecreasing. If rounded lateness differs it preserves order; if rounding ties the explicit third finish field orders f1 before f2.
For f1==f2: feasibility and lateness are equal, so identical tie tails break the tie identically.
Therefore the transform (f>D,max(0,f-D),f) preserves exactly the finish ordering, and argmin selects the identical resource for every valid allowed candidate set.

The public select_ready_task helper at742 also groups HEFT and deadline-aware HEFT in the same rank/deadline/arrival/identity ordering. Native immediate socket handling does not supply a hidden distinct multi-job deadline order.
